speaker: davy_gannet
text: Raleigh's home! Landed at Plymouth with a ship so deep in gold she'd hardly steer. I told you in February. And it'll hold fair.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You told me in February he was gone for gold. You have had the second half in your mouth ever since.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: And now I've spent it. Gold, Will. A ship that sat wrong in the water for the weight of it. The stairs had it before Paul's will.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The stairs have it biggest. That is your office. How many men have you spoken with who were on the ship?

speaker: davy_gannet
text: Spoken with? I have spoken with a man who had it from a lighter. That is near enough for a landing. It'll blow fair all week on the strength of it.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Hold the boat, Davy. Near enough for you is a third too large by the time it reaches a stall. I am walking up. I am not buying the gold.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nor I. If Paul's has it smaller, I shall keep the smaller. I am going for paper.

speaker: davy_gannet
text: Smaller. You'll spoil it. A waterman brings a thing home at full size, and a scholar pares it for his dinner.

speaker: george_bryan
text: Then let him get his dinner honestly. Off the step, Will. The hill is the same hill.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Hold your boat, Davy. I am not buying the gold.
